source_refs.note: Exercise 14.4 Q4 (i)-(ii), book p.290 (PDF 295). Answer key PDF 312: (i) 5/2, (ii) +-1, both correct (sympy). Solution book PDF 1272-1274 agrees.

blocks.prompt: 4 (i) Find the constant \(\alpha\) such that the vectors are coplanar: \(\underline{i} - \underline{j} + \underline{k}\), \(\underline{i} - 2\underline{j} - 3\underline{k}\) and \(3\underline{i} - \alpha \underline{j} + 5\underline{k}\).
blocks.explanation:
Is sawal mein ek vector ke andar ek anjaan constant \(\alpha\) hai, aur sharat yeh hai ke teeno vectors coplanar hon.
Diya kya hai? Teen vectors, jin mein se teesre mein \(\alpha\) hai.
Find kya karna hai? \(\alpha\) ki woh value jis par vectors ek plane mein aa jayen.
Rule kaunsa? Coplanar ka matlab triple product 0.
Plan: determinant \(\alpha\) ke saath expand karenge, jo ek simple equation degi; usay 0 ke barabar rakh kar solve karenge.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\underline{i} - \underline{j} + \underline{k}\), \(\underline{i} - 2\underline{j} - 3\underline{k}\), \(3\underline{i} - \alpha\underline{j} + 5\underline{k}\) coplanar hain.
Humein find karna hai: \(\alpha\).
Tareeqa: coplanar \(\Leftrightarrow\) scalar triple product \(= 0\) (14.4.5). Kyun? Ek plane mein pare teen vectors par bana dabba chapta hota hai, us ka volume 0 hai. To determinant 0 rakhne se \(\alpha\) ki equation mil jayegi.

Determinant likhein
\[\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & -2 & -3 \\ 3 & -\alpha & 5 \end{vmatrix}\]
Kyun: Har vector ek row hai. \(\alpha\) ko bilkul ek aam number ki tarah treat karein; bas us ki jagah letter likha rahega.

Row 1 se expand karein
\[= 1(-10 - 3\alpha) + 1(5 + 9) + 1(-\alpha + 6)\]
\[= 10 - 4\alpha\]
Kyun: Pehla minor \((-2)(5) - (-3)(-\alpha)\). Yahan \((-3)(-\alpha) = 3\alpha\) hai, to minor \(-10 - 3\alpha\) bana. Doosra minor \((1)(5) - (-3)(3) = 5 + 9 = 14\); entry \(-1\) aur beech ka minus sign mil kar \(+\) bane. Teesra minor \((1)(-\alpha) - (-2)(3) = -\alpha + 6\). Ab numbers ko numbers se jama kiya \((-10 + 14 + 6 = 10)\) aur \(\alpha\) wali terms ko alag \((-3\alpha - \alpha = -4\alpha)\).
Dhyan dein: \(-(-3\alpha)\) jaisi jagah sign ka hisaab bohat dhyan se karein.

0 ke barabar rakh kar solve karein
\[10 - 4\alpha = 0\]
\[\alpha = \dfrac{10}{4} = \dfrac{5}{2}\]
Kyun: Coplanar ki sharat yahi hai. \(4\alpha\) ko doosri taraf le gaye aur 4 se divide kiya, phir fraction ko chhota kiya.

Tasdeeq
\[-10 - \tfrac{15}{2} + 14 - \tfrac{5}{2} + 6 = 0 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: \(\alpha = \frac{5}{2}\) ko simplify karne se pehle wali lambi expansion mein rakha: \(-10 - 7.5 + 14 - 2.5 + 6 = 0\). Bilkul 0 aaya, is liye jawab sahi hai.
blocks.final_answer:
\(\alpha = \frac{5}{2}\)
Isi value par teesra vector pehle do ke plane mein aa jata hai.

blocks.prompt: 4 (ii) Find the constant \(\alpha\) such that the vectors are coplanar: \(\underline{i} - 2\alpha \underline{j} - \underline{k}\), \(\underline{i} - 2\underline{j} + 2\underline{k}\) and \(\alpha \underline{i} - 2\underline{j} + \underline{k}\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh part (i) jaisa hi hai, farq yeh hai ke \(\alpha\) ab do vectors mein aaya hai.
Diya kya hai? Teen vectors, pehle aur teesre mein \(\alpha\).
Find kya karna hai? \(\alpha\) ki saari values.
Rule kaunsa? Phir wohi: triple product \(= 0\).
Plan: determinant expand karne par \(\alpha^2\) wali quadratic equation banegi, is liye do jawab mil sakte hain.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\underline{i} - 2\alpha\underline{j} - \underline{k}\), \(\underline{i} - 2\underline{j} + 2\underline{k}\), \(\alpha\underline{i} - 2\underline{j} + \underline{k}\) coplanar hain.
Humein find karna hai: \(\alpha\).
Tareeqa: scalar triple product \(= 0\). Jab letter do rows mein ho to minors mein letters aapas mein multiply honge, is liye \(\alpha^2\) aa sakta hai; ghabrana nahi, yeh aasaan quadratic hogi.

Determinant likhein
\[\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & -2\alpha & -1 \\ 1 & -2 & 2 \\ \alpha & -2 & 1 \end{vmatrix}\]
Kyun: Har vector ki ek row, \(\underline{i}, \underline{j}, \underline{k}\) ki tarteeb mein.

Row 1 se expand karein
\[= 1(-2 + 4) + 2\alpha(1 - 2\alpha) - 1(-2 + 2\alpha)\]
\[= 2 + 2\alpha - 4\alpha^2 + 2 - 2\alpha\]
\[= 4 - 4\alpha^2\]
Kyun: Pehla minor \((-2)(1) - (2)(-2) = -2 + 4 = 2\). Doosra minor \((1)(1) - (2)(\alpha) = 1 - 2\alpha\); beech ki entry \(-2\alpha\) hai aur sign minus, to \(-(-2\alpha) = +2\alpha\). Teesra minor \((1)(-2) - (-2)(\alpha) = -2 + 2\alpha\), aur entry \(-1\) hai. Brackets kholne par \(+2\alpha\) aur \(-2\alpha\) cancel ho gaye aur sirf \(4 - 4\alpha^2\) bacha.

Solve karein
\[4 - 4\alpha^2 = 0\]
\[\alpha^2 = 1\]
\[\alpha = \pm 1\]
Kyun: 4 se divide kiya to \(\alpha^2 = 1\). Square root lene par dono signs aate hain, kyunke \(1^2\) aur \((-1)^2\) dono 1 hain.
Dhyan dein: Sirf \(\alpha = 1\) likh dena aur \(-1\) bhool jana aam ghalti hai; answer key bhi \(\pm 1\) deti hai.

Tasdeeq
\[\alpha = 1:\ \underline{i} - 2\underline{j} - \underline{k},\ \underline{i} - 2\underline{j} + 2\underline{k},\ \underline{i} - 2\underline{j} + \underline{k}\]
\[\alpha = -1:\ \alpha\underline{i} - 2\underline{j} + \underline{k} = -(\underline{i} + 2\underline{j} - \underline{k})\]
Kyun: \(\alpha = 1\) par har vector ka \(\underline{j}\) component us ke \(\underline{i}\) component ka \(-2\) guna hai, yani teeno plane \(y = -2x\) mein hain. \(\alpha = -1\) par teesra vector pehle ka bilkul ulta (negative) hai, yani dono ek hi line par hain; aur do vectors jo ek line par hon, teesre ke saath hamesha ek plane mein aa jate hain. Dono values sahi hain.
